A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Krause Synchronization Transformers and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained, relocated and newly added material can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-classification, autoregressive-generation and Llama/Qwen evaluation results, including component ablations and throughput measurements in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds language-model pretraining, LongBench evaluation and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The RBF affinity, local support, top-k selection and auxiliary language-model pathway remain unchanged. V3 adds a KViT variant replacing additive positional encoding with RoPE (Appendix D.2.4), constituting a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: V3 adds FineWeb-Edu and WikiText-103 for language-model training, plus LAMBADA, CBT, Blimp, Hellaswag and ARC-Easy evaluation. It also introduces 21 LongBench tasks covering bilingual long-context evaluation. Existing vision, generation and LoRA benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates RoPE and top-k ViT comparators, introduces sliding-window, top-k, Longformer and Routing Transformer language-model comparisons, and directly compares against a learnable sink token (Tables 8, 17–19, 25 and 27). The Swin comparison already existed in v2 Table 14 and is moved to v3 Table 4.

E3.justification: V3 introduces 100M/200M pretraining protocols using 10B/20B tokens and 1024-token sequences, adjusts baseline layer counts for parameter matching, and evaluates LongBench at 8K context. Existing ImageNet settings also change: learning rates are revised and Krause sigma changes from 4.0 to 4.5/9.0 (v2 Table 9; v3 Table 11).

E4.justification: V3 adds targeted analyses of positional-encoding compatibility and LongBench sensitivity to window/top-k settings of 32/16 versus 512/256 (Table 26). Existing vision component ablations, generation ablations and Llama/Qwen hyperparameter studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for pretraining, LongBench, RoPE/top-k comparisons and sink-token comparisons. ImageNet Table 3 is revised: ViT-B-16/KViT-B-16 accuracies change from 72.19/74.50 to 75.85/76.75 under changed training recipes, so these are not same-setting gains. Existing generation and LoRA benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, attention equations and Appendix C clustering arguments remain unchanged apart from punctuation and notation presentation. New Appendix E.3 discusses over-smoothing conceptually without adding a formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the empirical validation claim to language models trained from scratch at 100M/200M scales. The introduction revises the claimed average vision accuracy improvement from +3.7% to +3.0% across revised comparisons. The central bounded-confidence synchronization contribution remains the same.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of RoPE compatibility, the complementary role of compact local branches, and over-smoothing (D.2.4, D.4.4 and E.3). It also interprets the sink-token comparison as evidence for structural mitigation. Appendix A acknowledges pretraining experiments while retaining the limitation that language models still use standard attention.

D1.justification: New Table 14 documents pretraining budgets, optimizer settings, batching, sequence length, architecture, comparator-specific settings and H200 hardware. The ImageNet recipe is also revised and separated by model type in Table 11. These substantially expand the technical information beyond v2's vision, generation and LoRA recipes.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds substantive positioning against earlier distance-kernel attention, relative positional encoding, adaptive attention spans, Longformer, top-k attention and Routing Transformers. Appendix E.3 adds over-smoothing literature. These additions materially broaden discussion of closely related methods and theoretical perspectives.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in empirical summaries and selected experimental passages, with most existing prose retained. The Swin discussion moves into Section 5.2, and former Appendices E and F become E.1 and E.2 under a broader heading. The publication notice also changes.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the table displays with pretraining, extended-baseline, LongBench and sink-token tables, adds RoPE rows to Tables 1–3, and restructures the ImageNet configuration table. The Swin table moves into the main text. Figure 2 corrects masking notation and clarifies its caption; Figure 6 removes LoRA-specific labels.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v2's limited testing against close alternatives and its reliance on LoRA-only language evidence. Pretraining experiments, parameter-matched comparisons, 8K LongBench tests and RoPE/sink-token controls strengthen empirical validation, while new recipes improve reproducibility. Results are not uniformly favorable—the sink-token baseline wins on MMLU-Pro—and uncertainty estimates remain absent. Nevertheless, the broader controls and explicit retention of the global-attention limitation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
